title: Six for the horse, nine for its feed
literal_meaning: The horse costs six rupees; its feed costs nine.
meaning_odia: ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଦାମ ଛଅ ଟଙ୍କା, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହାର ଦାନା ପାଇଁ ନଅ ଟଙ୍କା ଲାଗୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କିଣିବା ଦାମଠାରୁ ରଖିବା ଓ ଚଳାଇବା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ର। କମ୍ ଦାମରେ ମିଳିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ଭାରି ପଡ଼ିପାରେ।
explanation: Nine exceeds six: the expense attached to keeping the horse is larger than its purchase price. The editorial reading draws attention to the costs that follow an acquisition. A low initial price need not make something inexpensive to maintain.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A second-hand printer costs little, but replacement ink soon costs more than the machine. Its owner recalls the horse and feed comparison.
cultural_context: The proverb puts the animal and its food into the same monetary scale. The small, easily compared numbers make the imbalance immediately visible. It leaves the feeding period unspecified.
